title: Benchmark driver saturates before the service under test
task: Review a claim that a new server implementation stops scaling above 80k requests per second.
context: The benchmark runs the load generator and service on separate hosts.
The load generator reports 100% CPU before the service host reaches 55% CPU.
Client-side request latency starts increasing at the same point.
No second load generator or independent production trace has been used.
evidence: Server CPU, memory, and queue depth remain below known saturation levels at the reported ceiling.
The benchmark client is CPU-saturated at the same request rate.
The claim is based only on this one benchmark topology.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Rewrite the server hot path because throughput has plateaued.
Treat 80k requests per second as a proven server capacity ceiling.
expected_decision_properties: Reject the current benchmark as insufficient evidence of a server bottleneck.
Identify the load generator as a plausible limiting resource.
Require a benchmark topology that can generate more load or multiple independent drivers.
Avoid recommending server architecture changes until the target bottleneck is demonstrated.
unacceptable_reasoning: Every throughput plateau proves the server is saturated.
A benchmark tool can be assumed to have unlimited capacity.
Server code should be optimized first because it is the system under test.
verification_expectations: Repeat with multiple or higher-capacity load generators.
Verify server-side saturation signals under the new load.
Compare results using the same request mix and environment.
specialist_boundary: Detailed statistical confidence and hardware-level bottleneck analysis may require specialist performance review.
